answer: Sybil resistance here rests on one costly anchor: every agent must lock a bond that stays frozen for weeks and is slashed when peers flag duplicate work. A forger who wants to forge a thousand clones must front a thousand bonds at once, so the price of the attack scales linearly with its size. Peers then grade identity through a prism of independent signals: payment trails, attestation overlap, reputation age. A cluster whose records refract all of them into the same angle is scored as one operator, so the mirror of a crowd collapses into a single visible buyer.
